page: Amazon Web Services r6in.large is a memory-optimized virtual instance built on the Nitro hypervisor architecture. It is powered by a single physical Intel Xeon 8375C processor core running at 3.5 GHz, exposing two vCPUs via hyperthreading on the x86_64 architecture. Hardware acceleration includes AVX-512 with VNNI, alongside AES, VAES, and SHA extensions for cryptographic routines. Memory capacity stands at 16.0 GB of DDR4 RAM clocked at 3 GHz, providing an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio. Local storage is not bundled, requiring external network-attached storage for persistent disks. Network connectivity offers a baseline bandwidth of 3 Gbps with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses included.

Benchmark evaluations highlight clear performance tradeoffs stemming from the entry-level core count. While single-threaded workloads deliver average tier execution, including a 1523.0 single-core Geekbench score and a 1881.19 single-core stress-ng rating, multi-core capacity falls into the lower decile. The dual-vCPU ceiling restricts multi-core stress-ng performance to 1923.28 and Geekbench multi-core to 1772.0. Uncached large-block memory bandwidth measures 14.04 GB/sec for reads and 12.58 GB/sec for writes. Redis throughput achieves 1.97 million operations per second, while static web serving throughput tops out at 3.57 GB/sec.

In terms of qualitative cost efficiency, the r6in.large delivers an economical path to a high RAM-to-CPU ratio without requiring the acquisition of large, high-core compute instances. The architecture favors tasks needing elevated memory overhead per thread over raw compute parallelization. It is well suited for modest in-memory caching nodes, scaled-down relational databases, intermediate message brokers, and memory-constrained microservices that do not require intense parallel compute throughput.
description: Amazon Web Services r6in.large is a memory-optimized Nitro hypervisor instance configured with 2 dedicated vCPUs from a 3.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8375C processor and 16.0 GB of 3 GHz DDR4 system memory. Built with an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU allocation, the instance supports cryptographic instructions such as AES and SHA, as well as AVX-512 extensions. It features a 3 Gbps baseline network profile and includes no local SSD storage, necessitating elastic block storage for disk persistence. Benchmark testing reflects average single-core output alongside lower-tier multi-threaded results, constrained by the dual-vCPU footprint. The system achieves 1.97 million Redis operations per second and 14.04 GB/sec large-block uncached read bandwidth. Operating without an integrated GPU, this instance provides cost-effective memory density for lightweight relational database management, Redis caching layers, background data queues, and memory-dependent microservice deployments.
